A.trend: Traced series with window and peak (2,127, Feb 2025). It quantifies late/early 0.32 and CAGR -67.5%, and gives critical late/early 0.30. The chart and text use selected months only, and there is no critical_pct series.
A.comparison: Tone ratio 8.09 vs a defined baseline of 0.58 (13.95x), early-vs-late thirds, and the monthly ratio range 3.68–20.93 all recompute. It does not compare dairy vs human.
A.chart: One traced line with window, unit and source, but only 9 of 24 months. There is no critical overlay or tone chart.
A.drilldown: Gives themes, taxonomy and entities, plus dated headlines with urls. Five of six follow-ups executed and cover the dairy and human facets.
A.export: Two traced CSVs and a provenance JSON. The monthly CSV is a subset of months, which caps this score.
A.repro: 88/88 numbers traced, there is a calls block with args, and derived numbers are recomputable (82.4%).
A.refs: Script ceiling of 1. The news items carry urls, but the benchmark cannot verify them.
A.accuracy: Fields are read correctly. It catches entity mislabels (cult of the dead cow, aceyalone, the who). It correctly notes May is not flagged partial and gets the geography window right.
A.limits: Window end, the 145-day gap, enrichment lag with fill percentages, match modes and the topic-vs-subject gap all sit next to the numbers. It names what would close each gap.
A.verdict: Direct answer with decision, confidence and reason, and what would change it. It does not name the Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 rebounds inside the verdict itself.
A.facets: Volume, trend, tone, themes, geography and headlines are grounded. Dairy and human counts are given as an explicit grounded 'no data' with proxies.

B.trend: Full 24-point traced series with peak, -95.9% from peak and late/early 32%. It has no critical decomposition.
B.comparison: Tone vs baseline is traced and recomputes, and the baseline is defined.
B.chart: Full traced volume chart only. There is no tone or critical facet, and the censored month is not marked.
B.drilldown: There is no traced item layer: no headlines or urls. Only 2 of 6 follow-ups executed.
B.export: Full monthly CSV with provenance block, but it is the only table.
B.repro: 21/22 traced and the calls block has args.
B.accuracy: Calls May 2026 a 'partial, censored ingest month'. The reference has partial_period false and censoring at 2026-06-01.
B.limits: Window, gap, match modes, sample and classifier limits are stated. Some sit in a footer.
B.verdict: Clear answer, decision, confidence and conditions.
B.facets: Dairy and human facets are named as unmeasurable, but there are no headlines or proxies. Themes are thin.

C.limits: States what is missing but nothing about specific windows.
C.drilldown: Follow-ups use invalid args. None executed.

D.trend: Memory herd estimate, labelled, not coverage.
D.comparison: Memory herds vs human cases on non-equivalent units.
D.accuracy: Event facts are broadly plausible and labelled est.
D.verdict: Does not answer the coverage question. Gives low confidence with a reason.

B: States May 2026 is a partial/censored month; reference marks partial_period false (censoring is at 2026-06-01).
D: Herd counts and human case figures are from memory, unverified (labelled est.).

raw.verdict: A and B both read the measured series correctly: bird-flu coverage peaked in Feb 2025 and is falling. A went further. It quantified the critical-share trend, gave dated headlines with urls, caught entity mislabels, and honestly flagged that dairy and human coverage was not isolated. B was cleaner on the full series but thinner on drill-down and slightly misread censoring. C refused, and D offered labelled memory about the outbreak rather than coverage.
